- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price drop is steep.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–4% for 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted price.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” (strong bullish) followed by “0.00” (bearish), model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
